4.text: On the whole, in all strife and cases of revenge the rights of the paternal

5.text: line are decidedly preponderant over those of the maternal. In case the

6.text: interests of other groups come into collision, a man has to stay with the

7.text: paternal line. The same is true for the Asiatic Eskimo. The people at

8.text: Indian Point declared, “In the case of a quarrel, the father’s kin becomes

9.text: near, and the mother’s remote.” Still, the saying, that, in case of need, even

10.text: the remotest relation may appear as an avenger, is occasionally put into

11.text: practice. For instance, when a Chukchee man was killed by the Russians

12.text: at the Anui fair in 1895, an incident, of which I have already spoken, the

13.text: wrong was taken up, first of all, by the step-father of the killed one; i. e.,

14.text: by a man who was not connected with him on either the paternal or maternal

15.text: side. He negotiated with the officials, and even received the first portion of

16.text: the pay for the blood. It seemed, however, that he was conscious of having

17.text: no right to that pay: at least, some of it was stolen from him almost im-

18.text: mediately by the other Chukchee. He offered to return the remainder to the

19.text: Russians under the pretense that they should keep it for the brother of the

20.text: slain. In the end, of course, he took it for himself.

21.text: From this moment, day after day, various Chukchee from the Chaun

22.text: country came to the Russian officials. Some of them declared themselves to

23.text: be cousins of the killed one, how many times removed nobody could ascertain.

24.text: The others simply said that they were his fellow-countrymen. They explained,

25.text: “We have trodden the same ground as he. This is sufficient to make us

26.text: feel compassion at his death.” Most of them also declared that it was their

27.text: intention to get some part of the pay for blood; but the others only offered

28.text: a lot of invective, even threatening the Russian officer to his very face. After

29.text: that they would go. Still all of them declared that all these doings were

30.text: quite useless, and that revenge would not begin until the next year, when the

31.text: brother of the victim would come to the fair.

32.text: Nevertheless, there are cases where no kinsman wants to appear as an

33.text: avenger of blood. Of brothers and cousins there may be none; and the more

34.text: remote relations do not care to take up the quarrel, especially if the hostile
